extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scientists, and students of method interested in principles for discovering and validating knowledge
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for discovering and validating natural knowledge by careful induction from particulars, guarding against mental idols and methodological shortcuts; aimed at reforming philosophical and scientific method. Focuses on experimental aids, careful definition, and progressive ascent to axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin from the senses and particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Our method ... consists in determining the degrees of certainty, while we, as it were, restore the senses to their former rank, but generally reject that operation of the mind which follows close upon the senses, and open and establish a new and certain course for the mind from the first actual perceptions of the senses themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start inquiry with careful attention to observed particulars and sensory perception rather than leaping immediately to abstract generalities. Collect and arrange particular instances in regular series; treat the senses as primary data for induction. Anti-pattern: beginning from abstract axioms or allowing immediate mental interpretations to override observed particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascend gradually to axioms (true induction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The other constructs its axioms from the senses and particulars, by ascending continually and gradually, till it finally arrives at the most general axioms, which is the true but unattempted way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive general principles only after systematically assembling and interrogating many diverse particulars; avoid the opposite 'hurry' from few senses to the most general axioms. Scoring note: strong work demonstrates the stepwise ascent with clear chains of instances supporting each inferred generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject anticipations (rash premature generalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: We call that human reasoning which we apply to nature the anticipation of nature (as being rash and premature) … Anticipations are sufficiently powerful in producing unanimity ... Anticipations will be assented to much more readily than interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not impose preconceived notions or speculative generalities on observations. Beware of hypotheses asserted as principles without being constructed from varied particulars. Anti-pattern: forcing data to fit admired theories or favoring elegant axioms over empirical grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use instruments and mechanical aids for the understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects are produced by the means of instruments and helps, which the understanding requires no less than the hand; ... If men ... had attempted mechanical labors with their hands alone ... they would have been able to move and overcome but little ... just to pause awhile on this comparison ... the understanding requires instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ experimental apparatus, methodological devices, and procedural schemes to extend the power of observation and control. Treat instruments as essential aids to discovery, not mere accessories. Example: design experiments and tools that reveal otherwise inaccessible particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer experiment and fit instances over syllogistic logic for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The syllogism is not applied to the principles of the sciences, and is of no avail in intermediate axioms ... The present system of logic rather assists in confirming and rendering inveterate the errors founded on vulgar notions than in searching after truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use logical deduction for exposition and testing, but rely on carefully structured experiments and induction to produce new scientific principles. Anti-pattern: relying primarily on syllogistic argument to discover new effects rather than empirical testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and guard against the four idols (biases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four species of idols beset the human mind ... calling the first Idols of the Tribe, the second Idols of the Den, the third Idols of the Market, the fourth Idols of the Theatre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly consider cognitive and social biases when evaluating observations and inferences: Idols of the Tribe (human nature and common sense error), Den (individual prejudice/habit), Market (confusions from language and popular discourse), Theatre (systematic philosophical dogmas). Anti-pattern: failing to reflect on how these idols distort interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give weight to negative instances (negatives are powerful)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the peculiar and perpetual error of the human understanding to be more moved and excited by affirmatives than negatives, whereas it ought duly and regularly to be impartial; nay, in establishing any true axiom the negative instance is the most powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat counterexamples and failures as critical tests that can invalidate or refine axioms; prioritize systematic searches for negatives as part of induction. Scoring note: robust arguments anticipate and address negative instances explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct axioms from many and varied instances, not a scanty handful
rubrics_metrics.description: The axioms now in use are derived from a scanty handful, as it were, of experience, and a few particulars of frequent occurrence ... And if any neglected or unknown instance occurs, the axiom is saved by some frivolous distinction, when it would be more consistent with truth to amend it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base generalizations on broad, heterogeneous datasets that probe peripheral, rare, and countervailing cases. Avoid saving hypotheses with ad hoc distinctions when new instances appear. Anti-pattern: invoking special pleading to preserve a favored axiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissect matter and actions rather than rely on abstract forms
rubrics_metrics.description: It is better to dissect than abstract nature: such was the method employed by the school of Democritus ... It is best to consider matter, its conformation, and the changes of that conformation, its own action, and the law of this action or motion; for forms are a mere fiction of the human mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concrete mechanisms, configurations, and lawful actions of parts rather than metaphysical 'forms'. Prefer analyses of processes and laws of action in experiments. Example: study particle interactions and changes in conformation rather than invoking vague qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about words and definitions (idols of the Market)
rubrics_metrics.description: Words are formed at the will of the generality, and there arises from a bad and unapt formation of words a wonderful obstruction to the mind ... For men imagine that their reason governs words, while, in fact, words react upon the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define terms precisely using regular series of instances; do not let conventional or ambiguous language obscure distinctions. Anti-pattern: treating poorly defined terms (e.g., 'moist', 'dense') as if precise, leading to confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate attention between particulars and general composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The contemplation of nature and of bodies in their individual form distracts and weakens the understanding; but the contemplation of nature and of bodies in their general composition and formation stupefies and relaxes it. These two species of contemplation must, therefore, be interchanged, and each employed in its turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotate methodological focus: sometimes investigate fine distinctions among particulars, other times study broader patterns—both are necessary for balanced understanding. Anti-pattern: exclusive focus on either micro particulars or abstract generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct preoccupied habits of mind by deliberate hesitation and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever may be desirous of forming any determination upon an opinion of this our work ... will not expect to be able to do so in a cursory manner ... will correct the depraved and deeply rooted habits of his mind by a seasonable, and, as it were, just hesitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate intellectual discipline: avoid snap judgments, train oneself in patient observation and regulated doubt. Scoring note: methodology that documents iterative self-correction and training in recognizing biases is stronger.

rubrics_metrics.name: An instauration from foundations is required for true progress
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in vain to expect any great progress in the sciences by the superinducing or ingrafting new matters upon old. An instauration must be made from the very foundations, if we do not wish to revolve forever in a circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to question and replace foundational methods and assumptions rather than only adding ad hoc fixes. Anti-pattern: layering new results onto an unsound methodological base without reexamining core practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware the human tendency to invent unwarranted order
rubrics_metrics.description: The human understanding, from its peculiar nature, easily supposes a greater degree of order and equality in things than it really finds; ... Hence the fiction, that all celestial bodies move in perfect circles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume symmetry, perfect forms, or neat regularities without empirical support. Seek evidence for proposed orders rather than preferring aesthetically pleasing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that present sciences often arrange known matters rather than discover new effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the effects already discovered are due to chance and experiment rather than to the sciences; for our present sciences are nothing more than peculiar arrangements of matters already discovered, and not methods for discovery or plans for new operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methods by their capacity to produce novel discoveries, not merely to systematize existing facts. Scoring note: methods that enable discovery of previously unknown effects are valued higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent confirmation by logic alone (logic can confirm errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The present system of logic rather assists in confirming and rendering inveterate the errors founded on vulgar notions than in searching after truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat purely deductive coherence as insufficient; seek empirical tests that could falsify inferred conclusions. Anti-pattern: privileging internally consistent argumentation while ignoring counterevidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer severe regulations and authority to enforce consideration of heterogeneous instances
rubrics_metrics.description: The human understanding is most excited by that which strikes and enters the mind at once ... it is very slow and unfit for the transition to the remote and heterogeneous instances by which axioms are tried as by fire, unless the office be imposed upon it by severe regulations and a powerful authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement methodological controls (protocols, systematic testing, institutional practices) that force consideration of diverse and remote instances. Example: require explicit tests against peripheral cases before accepting generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect and suspect whatever particularly takes and fixes the understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: He who contemplates nature should suspect whatever particularly takes and fixes his understanding, and should use so much the more caution to preserve it equable and unprejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a researcher feels unusually attracted to a hypothesis or dataset, apply extra scrutiny for personal bias. Anti-pattern: equating intellectual fascination with correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regular series and arrangement of particular instances to determine notions and axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring men to particulars and their regular series and order, and they must for a while renounce their notions, and begin to form an acquaintance with things ... we must necessarily have recourse to particular instances, and their regular series and arrangement, as we shall mention when we come to the mode and scheme of determining notions and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize observed instances into ordered series (varying one factor at a time, combinatorial lists, gradations) so that generalizations emerge from patterns across well-structured sets of particulars. Scoring note: clear presentation of ordered instances supporting a claimed axiom is central to evaluating rigor.
